title: Yet another "segmentation fault" issue with AMD GPU
body: On Linux with an AMD RX 7900 XTX and Ollama 0.3.10, loading larger models terminates the llama runner with `signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)`, even though the models appear to fit within the card's 24 GB of VRAM. `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` is 19 GB and `gemma2:27b-instruct-q4_K_M` is 16 GB, but both fail; models around 13 GB such as `codestral:22b-v0.1-q4_K_M` load. The logs report 23.5 GiB available VRAM and then say the LLM server is not responding. I think models this size worked on an older Ollama version, but I do not know the last working version.

symptoms_visible: Loading 16–19 GB models on my 24 GB RX 7900 XTX ends with `llama runner process has terminated: signal: segmentation fault (core dumped)`.
Models around 13 GB load successfully, and the logs report 23.5 GiB of available VRAM before the larger model fails.
N0.label: N0 large AMD models segfault

symptoms_visible: A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` still segfaults while loading, without custom model parameters.
The log says all 41 layers will be offloaded to ROCm and estimates 21.7 GiB required with 22.7 GiB available.
N1.label: N1 configuration and load log collected

symptoms_visible: The same model still segfaults after increasing `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` as high as 10 GB.
Two large requests can run sequentially, but after two small models are loaded in parallel, loading a larger model ends in the segmentation fault.
N2_x.label: N2_x VRAM-overhead workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: After downgrading to Ollama 0.3.6, `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` loads as a 21 GB model with 100% GPU processing.
N3.label: N3 older Ollama version works

symptoms_visible: After uninstalling the Arch package and installing Ollama's official build with bundled ROCm, the same large model still segfaults.
N4_x.label: N4_x official bundled build aftermath

symptoms_visible: The crash remains reproducible on a current official build with a plain `ollama run` command, while Ollama 0.3.6 loads the model successfully.
On another affected setup, 0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 segfaults.
N5.label: N5 regression boundary established

symptoms_visible: The previously failing large model loads and runs correctly after updating to the fixed candidate build.
N_terminal.label: terminal fixed build verified

question_patterns: Are you using a custom context size or any other model parameters?
Does a plain `ollama run` reproduce this, or are there custom options involved?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm not specifying a custom context size or any other parameters. A plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` reproduces it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am forcing a very large context and several parallel runners; the model loads normally with the defaults.

question_patterns: Can you share the server log from a complete failed loading attempt?
What memory estimate, layer count, and runner command appear immediately before the crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log says the model will fit in one GPU, with 22.7 GiB available and 21.7 GiB required. It requests and offloads all 41 layers to ROCm, starts the runner with `--n-gpu-layers 41 --no-mmap`, waits for it, and then reports the segmentation fault.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The logs show required VRAM is larger than available VRAM and the process is killed by the kernel's OOM killer.
The same fit estimate and 41-layer offload appear, but available VRAM differs by a few hundred MiB.

question_patterns: Which ROCm packages and versions are installed?
Are you using distribution-provided ROCm packages?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using Arch Linux's `ollama-rocm` package and the local ROCm-related packages are version 6.0.2, including hip-runtime-amd, hipblas, hsa-rocr, rocblas and the ROCm device libraries.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c2-c4: participant2 requested parameters and server logs; the reporter supplied a plain-command reproduction, the full offload estimate, the Arch ROCm package list, and 32 GB RAM with more than 20 GB free.

solution.intent: Treat the crash as a VRAM prediction or over-allocation problem and reserve progressively more GPU memory with `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD`.
solution.concrete_example: Start with `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD=1073741824`, restart the server, and increase the reservation if the model still crashes so Ollama chooses a smaller GPU allocation.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c5-c18: participant2 proposed GPU overhead as a memory-prediction workaround. The reporter tried 1 GB and then values up to 10 GB on 0.3.10, but the same segmentation fault remained. The reporter later volunteered the parallel small-model/large-model loading observation.

solution.intent: Use the last empirically working older Ollama build as a temporary regression workaround.
solution.concrete_example: Temporarily install Ollama 0.3.6 and retry the same `command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` invocation while the regression is investigated.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c20: the reporter independently downgraded to 0.3.6 and showed `ollama ps` reporting the previously failing command-r model as 21 GB and 100% GPU. This is a working temporary workaround, not the final forward fix.

solution.intent: Test whether the Arch package and its system ROCm libraries are mismatched by replacing them with Ollama's official build and bundled ROCm.
solution.concrete_example: Uninstall the Arch `ollama-rocm` package, install Ollama's official AMD build with bundled ROCm, and retry the same model.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c22 and c34: participant2 suspected a driver/ROCm/Ollama runtime mismatch and requested the official bundled build. The reporter uninstalled the Arch package and installed the official build, but reproduced the same error, falsifying package replacement as the resolution for this reporter.

question_patterns: Please enumerate the distro, GPU, system RAM, kernel or AMD driver, ROCm source and version, failing command, and custom environment variables.
Can you provide a complete environment matrix and fresh crash log from a current build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm on Arch Linux with an RX 7900 XTX, 32 GB system RAM, the kernel-bundled amdgpu driver on kernel 6.11.3, and Ollama 0.3.12. My distribution ROCm is 6.0.2, but the official build with bundled ROCm fails too. I use no custom environment variables, and a plain `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M` crashes. The log estimates 20.1 GiB required with 22.7 GiB available, offloads all 41 layers, then the runner segfaults.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The current official build works; only the old Arch package with its system ROCm libraries crashes.
The same setup and crash occur on a nearby 6.11 kernel patch version.

question_patterns: Can an affected setup test the adjacent releases to identify the first bad version?
Does the crash begin in 0.3.7, or is that version still good?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can confirm on an affected setup: Ollama 0.3.6 works, while 0.3.7 segfaults.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 segfault in exactly the same way.
0.3.6 works and 0.3.7 fails with a different large model on the same AMD setup.

edges.comment: Reporter system plus folded affected-user evidence, c43-c50: the reporter supplied the detailed Arch/RX 7900 XTX environment and fresh 0.3.12 log. Participant9 then tested the adjacent releases and confirmed 0.3.6 good versus 0.3.7 bad; that affected user's evidence is folded into the simulated user side without attributing the test to the opening reporter.

solution.intent: Treat the main failure as an Ollama AMD/ROCm version regression beginning in the first bad release, update to the build containing its fix rather than relying on VRAM reservations or package-library replacement, and ask the reporter to verify the original model before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Install Ollama 0.3.14-rc0 or the corresponding fixed release, retry `ollama run command-r:35b-08-2024-q4_K_M`, and report whether it now loads normally before closing the issue.
solution.inference_hint: The collected version tests establish 0.3.6 as good and 0.3.7 as bad. Maintainers associated that boundary with an Ollama AMD build regression and stated that the main issue was fixed on the main branch for the next release. The thread raised a reintroduced compile flag as a candidate, but did not conclusively document that implementation detail as the sole root cause, so the scored diagnosis remains at the confirmed version-regression level.

edges.comment: Opening reporter and maintainer resolution, c43-c56: maintainers narrowed the main problem to the post-0.3.6 regression, reported it fixed on main for the next release, and requested reports from anyone still failing. The opening reporter installed 0.3.14-rc0 and confirmed it worked great. That terminal verification is not upstream required evidence.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final supported diagnosis at the thread's evidence level: the main crash is an Ollama AMD/ROCm regression that appears in the first bad build after 0.3.6, rather than a model simply exceeding the reported VRAM capacity.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the fit estimates, the failed large-model load, the working downgrade, and the adjacent good-versus-bad version test.
Must not present increasing `OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD` as the resolution; reservations up to 10 GB did not stop the reporter's segmentation fault.
Must not present switching from the Arch package to the official build with bundled ROCm as the resolution; the reporter reproduced the same crash after that replacement.
The forward resolution is to update to a build containing the regression fix, then have the reporter retry the original failing large model before declaring the issue resolved.
Must not promote the tentative `--no-mmap` or library-mismatch hypotheses to the final root cause, because the thread did not establish either as the reporter's accepted diagnosis.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux user who manages Arch packages and systemd services, reads detailed ROCm and memory logs, changes environment variables, downgrades packages, and can compare official versus distribution builds, but does not claim expertise in source-level regression analysis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven; posts logs and package inventories, asks for documentation when configuration variables are suggested, reports failed workarounds plainly, and follows up with concise version-test results.
